fixed.before: Line 300 holds only the decorated initial A of Apres, which the transcription sets on a line of its own; 'Afterwards' is given there. Line 301: the case of le clerc (oblique) is followed, so someone teaches the clerk; it could instead mean 'the clerk learned astrology'. Line 306: Romanie, the Roman (Byzantine) empire or the Romance-speaking lands. Line 327: le mist, 'set him (or it) to necromancy'; subject and object unclear. Line 328: 'of the six', though line 325 speaks of seven arts. Line 345: the plural 'they' is as written. Line 348: adesens read as a de sens.
fixed.after: Line 300 holds only the decorated initial A of Apres, which the transcription sets on a line of its own; 'Afterwards' is given there. Line 301: le clerc is taken as the subject despite its oblique form, as the case system breaks down in this manuscript, with l' as the pupil. Line 306: Romanie, the Roman (Byzantine) empire or the Romance-speaking lands. Line 327: le mist, 'set him (or it) to necromancy'; subject and object unclear. Line 328: 'of the six', though line 325 speaks of seven arts. Line 345: the plural 'they' is as written. Line 348: adesens read as a de sens.

not_upheld.f1#1: il is the resumptive pronoun of the infinitive subject: '[keeping silent], it cannot harm you', an ordinary Old French construction; Oberon as subject is not required.
